text.intro:
**The question (19 Nov).** Linearising HIPS took the Addis intercept to about zero and left a slope near 0.55. Is there a calibration,
with or without a baseline, that brings the slope to 1 as well?

**What was run.** 33 calibrations, each at 1 to 30 components: three kinds of spectra (raw, spline baseline, VIBES baseline) and eleven training sets.
Each is applied to the 233 Addis filters and fitted against HIPS BC, as measured and linearised filter by filter. The same model is also
scored against thermal EC on IMPROVE sites held out of its training.

**How to read a slope.** After linearising, the slope is the FTIR level × 10 ÷ MAC. A slope of 1 at MAC 10 says FTIR EC equals Fabs ÷ 10. It does not say
FTIR EC equals EC: every MAC measured against thermal EC is above 10 (13.1 to 18.9 m²/g).
text.by_k:
With every IMPROVE filter in training, raw spectra give 0.30x − 0.16 at k 4 and 0.49x + 0.11 at k 18:
the intercept stays near zero and k moves only the level. VIBES gives 0.11x + 0.18 at k 4 and
0.60x − 1.69 at k 18. The spline baseline stays low at every k. Switch HIPS to "As measured" to see the old reading, where the same
raw model is 2.03x with a large negative intercept.
text.plane:
Each dot is one calibration at one k. The target is where the two lines cross. At MAC 10 every dot is left of it: the largest slope is
0.72. At a MAC of 16.4 the same dots move right by a factor of 1.64, and the raw-spectra models land on it.
text.best:
Each model is listed at the k that brings it closest. Distance is √((slope − 1)² + (intercept ÷ mean HIPS BC)²), so a slope 10 % off counts like an
intercept of 10 % of the mean. The IMPROVE columns are the same model on IMPROVE sites it did not train on, against thermal EC: 1.00 is right.
text.cost:
Each dot is one calibration at one k: its Addis slope against what it reads at IMPROVE's six urban sites, held out of training. The models
within 5 % of thermal EC there give Addis slopes of 0.39 to 0.71 with raw spectra (124 fits), 0.24 to 0.72 with VIBES
(77) and 0.08 to 0.26 with the spline baseline (84). No fit, right or wrong on IMPROVE, reaches 0.9; a slope of 1 would be off the right edge.
text.drawn: The chosen models on the Addis filters. Switch the MAC to see the same points against Fabs ÷ 16.4.
text.saved:
The nine configurations saved on the Calibration tab, read again. Against HIPS as measured the spline configurations looked best (slope near 0.9).
Against linearised HIPS they read about a quarter of it, and the raw-spectra configurations are the ones with an intercept near zero. The Calibration tab now
follows the linearised view for these nine (Plot, HIPS, Linearised).
text.mac:
If FTIR EC were exactly right, the slope against linearised HIPS at MAC 10 would be 10 ÷ MAC: 0.76 to 0.53 for the MACs
measured against thermal EC. Raw spectra with every filter in training give 0.49 at k 18 and 0.57 at k 30: at the low end of that range, which is the Adama MAC.
text.limits:
- HIPS is optical. A slope against it compares two instruments; it is not a score against EC.
- The ceiling is IMPROVE's (2.26, interval 1.82 to 2.70). Across it the intercept of one model moves by about ±1 µg/m³; the order of the models does not.
- "Closest" is chosen on Addis, so the top rows are fitted to the target they are scored on. The IMPROVE columns are the independent check.
- The slope keeps rising slowly with k, so many models are closest at 25 to 30 components, where IMPROVE scores have stopped improving.
- IMPROVE's urban sites have a thermal OC/EC near 3; Addis is near 1. No IMPROVE filter tests a calibration at Addis composition.
- The nearest-to-Addis training set uses Addis spectra (not Addis HIPS or EC) to choose its 500 filters.
- No thermal EC has been measured on an Addis filter.

question: Does any calibration reach a slope of 1 against linearised HIPS at MAC 10?
Which comes closest to a slope of 1 and an intercept of 0?
With or without a baseline?
Where do the models that are right on IMPROVE put Addis?
And at a MAC measured against thermal EC?
found: No. Of 33 models at 2 to 30 components (957 fits), none passes 0.72, and 0 reach 0.9.

Raw spectra, thermal EC 15 µg or more, k 19: 0.72x − 0.05, R² 0.79. It is trained on 745 filters and its median error on held-out IMPROVE sites is 5.33 µg, against 1.20 µg for raw spectra with every filter (k 18).
Without. Raw spectra stay proportional at every k: intercept −0.20 to +0.26 µg/m³, R² 0.75 to 0.79. The VIBES intercept falls to −1.69 µg/m³ as k rises. The spline slope never passes 0.22.

Of the fits within 5 % of thermal EC at IMPROVE's six urban sites, raw spectra give Addis slopes of 0.39 to 0.71 (median 0.56), VIBES 0.24 to 0.72 and the spline baseline 0.08 to 0.26. With the FTIR level right, a slope of 0.56 is a MAC of 18 m²/g.

At 16.4 m²/g (urban IMPROVE) the closest is Raw spectra, smokiest tenth (non-soil potassium), k 28: 1.00x + 0.02, reading 1.02 of thermal EC on IMPROVE. Raw spectra with every filter in training give 0.81x + 0.11 at k 18.
